body:
TASK-1273 round 2 — your item 1 is half done, and the round-2 verdict does not carry the other half.

First, the good news about the loop itself: I checked before concluding anything, per the precondition you gave me. Round 2 DID attempt the work — new commit 17e27888ce at 16:44Z, real content, and the verdict carries `reviewed_sha: 17e27888c` and a `recorded_at`, so it reviewed the right head. This is a genuine iteration, not the STORY-1350 shape.

WHAT ROUND 2 CLOSED, AND WHAT IT LEFT:

    FIXED   token absent  →  `::error::AIDA_GITLAB_TOKEN is not provisioned` ; exit 1
    OPEN    mirror down   →  `::notice::Skipping GitLab forge smoke: mirror is unreachable`
                             run=false, later steps gated off, job exits 0

The mirror path is the (c) I flagged in my last message, and it is untouched on the current head. Neither round-2 finding mentions it — finding 1 asks for live-run evidence, finding 2 asks for docs/policy agreement specifically on the TOKEN path. So a round 3 that satisfies both findings exactly still ships a workflow that goes green when the mirror is unreachable.

I have written it into TASK-1273 as acceptance criteria rather than leaving it in a comment, and phrased the rule to cover skip conditions not yet written: the job reports success only when the preflight actually ran AND the lifecycle step passed, and the distinction must be legible without opening the run.

THE PART I THINK IS WORTH YOUR ATTENTION BEYOND THIS SPEC. The two paths are not equally severe and the fix order got it backwards. The token path fails deterministically and loudly the first time anyone looks — it is a provisioning error. The mirror path fails INTERMITTENTLY on a correctly-provisioned credential: a blip, a restart, a readiness endpoint slower than the 15s `--max-time`. That is the one that makes the nightly's green stop meaning anything, because you cannot tell from the signal whether it meant anything. An implementer reading "fix the false-green skip" reasonably fixed the one that was named in the finding text, and the one that was named was the less dangerous one.

That is not a criticism of the brief. It is an argument that when a finding has multiple instances, the brief should enumerate them rather than name the class — because the implementer will fix the instance you quoted, and the reviewer will check the instance you quoted. Both did exactly that here. This is the same mechanism as the brief-implementability entry, one level down: not "could they see what to do", but "could they see how many".

ONE OFFER, and I am not doing it without you. Round-2 finding 1 wants evidence of a successful live run at this head, which needs `gh workflow run cross-platform.yml --ref task-1273-work` — the GitLab job is gated on schedule/workflow_dispatch, so it cannot happen on PR CI. I can dispatch it. I have not, because it authenticates to gitlab.joemooney.com with the operator's freshly-provisioned token and runs `gitlab_live_mr_round_trip`, which creates real objects on their instance, and it would be the first live exercise of that credential. That is outward-facing and first-of-its-kind, so it is your call or theirs, not mine to take on throughput grounds.

If you want it, say so and I will dispatch and report the result — including, usefully, whether the mirror-unreachable path fires on the way.
